questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to travel and study at a good university that had a lot of different courses you could read but also to a place I have not been before, Australia and UQ was a great opportunity for that. Also a country where the spoken language is english was important.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Just great school, fun subject but also very chill, great campus, such a nice city and the people where also so nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was ok easy, you got most of the info you needed beforehand, both from KU and UQ, and the student central at the campus helped you with most stuff. Tbh the intro week was great to understand how everything works and where to find what.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a exchange student gathering where they talked about being on an exchange program at the school which was great and you got to meet others aswell. Other than that you had to reach out to your teachers or look online for stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was ok easy. I found my housing via other KU student going to UQ aswell, it was called Westella. Recommend! If you would be up for living in a big house with other exchange students, it was an amazing experience and really made my whole exchange, friends for life and always people you could hang out with and travel with etc. Otherwise there was something called Flatmates, where you could find apartment etc that you could share with others.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would recommen, since you will be spending a lot of your time on campus either way.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Most was online to just create and account and log in etc, UQ had a pretty solid step-through-step, that will show you what to do.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, it was pretyy straight forward. You will recieve emails and info online on where to log in and create a school email, and then you will basically only use their version of kunet and absalon to check news or course information.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The school offered a lot of help, that you could find both online or directly at campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty successful, there were a lot of options. You have to find the courses within the different bachelors/programs where they will have descriptions etc. I registered first for 4 courses, and then wanted to change one of them, which was also very easy to do in the UQ portal, you have ish a month after the courses start to change without "being charged". I got the course change confirmed from KU within a week aswell so it all went pretty smooth.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read about the different courses first, and what they offer cause there are so many! And look within the different faculties rather than bachelor programs, cause it will sort it out way more for you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: most of them were pretty easy, so it was just very chill.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Most of the courses I took where for first year students, and it was very easy. I took Communication across cultures (COMU1002), Multimedia (COMU1140), Design Computing Studio I (DECO1800) and Psychology of Communication (PSYC1100). I mostly liked Communication across cultures, it felt the most practical learning, and Design Computing Studio was fun, more programming which is what I wanted to do more.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was generally very strict for student to show up to class. Being absent multiple times could effect your grade, which is quite different from KU. It was also more small tasks with very strcit deadlines that needed to be done, and that the final exams usually was only around 30% of your grade, and the tasks along the way was just as important.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Communication across cultures (COMU1002), Multimedia (COMU1140), Design Computing Studio I (DECO1800) and Psychology of Communication (PSYC1100).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I mostly liked Communication across cultures, it felt the most practical learning, and Design Computing Studio was fun, more programming which is what I wanted to do more.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really unexpected, but traveling around Australia was the major cost. Going on trips during the spring break or after the semester, and then joining the social clubs at school and go on weekend trips with them.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The public transport in Queensland costs 50 cents per travel, which was very nice. Generally, the food prices or going to cafes etc was the same as Copenhagen, only the coffee was cheaper, around 40 DKK per.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Literally anything you could think of. Most of them were free to join, other you had to pay a small fee, like 10 AUD, and they had a "Market Day" during the Orientation Week where you can visit and talk to all the different clubs and join whichever you want.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just do all the stuff that you wouldn't/couldn't at home. I joined the climbing/mountain hiking club, surfing club, diving club and went on weekend trips and parties with all of them which was so nice. Joing QUEST, the exchange student socila club, you meet so many nice people and they orgnise the best weekend trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit as much as possible. Soem weekend trips we did were to Hervey Bay, Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast, Noosa, Moreton Island, Stradebroke Island etc. During the spring break we went to Cairns/Port Douglas and drove down, we went scubadiving, visited the rainforest etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. Australians are very relaxed and super friendly. I lived in a house of only exchange student so there weren't any Australians I hung out with daily in my home.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Tbh, just eat lunch together or go for a coffee or study break after, its easy to meet new people during the classes. Otherwise student clubs are the best option to find people with common interests.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really culture, but the heat could be unbearable sometimes. Maybe that soemtimes it was a little bit too relaxed, like sometimes stuff didn't get done etc. But generally all pretty smooth.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness of the people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Join different social clubs at the school, thats how you will make friends and do the best trips. Know beforehand what tasks and exams you will have and when during the semester in your different courses, it does sneak up on you. just try as much new things as possible because it goes by so fast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people I got to meet along the way that made my year abroad. Also being able to practice my english

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing home, saying goodbye to everyone

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
